property_summary: For any valid input that does not cause a revert, the reference `transfer` always returns `true`, while the buggy version can return `false` when the transaction succeeds.
For any admissible input where the call does not revert, P.transfer returns true while M.transfer returns false.
For any admissible input that does not cause a revert, the reference transfer returns true; the mutant returns false for the same successful calls.
Only the original hardcoded sender can successfully invoke transfer; the buggy contract allows a different sender to succeed.

For any admissible input, a call to transfer from any address other than the original required sender must revert; the mutant relaxes the sender check and thus allows a different caller to succeed without revert.

For any admissible input, a call to transfer from any msg.sender other than the original required address (0x9797...) must revert; the mutant relaxes the sender check and thus allows a different caller to succeed without revert.

For any admissible input, a call to transfer from any sender other than the original required address 0x9797... must revert; the mutant changes the required sender to 0x1f84... and therefore reverts for the old sender and succeeds for other senders, violating the rule that only the original sender succeeds.

For any admissible input, a call to transfer from any msg.sender other than the original required sender 0x9797055B68C5DadDE6b3c7d5D80C9CFE2eecE6c9 must revert; the mutant changes the required sender to 0x1f844685f7Bf86eFcc0e74D8642c54A257111923, so it reverts for the old sender but succeeds for the new sender, violating the rule.

Only the privileged sender 0x9797055B68C5DadDE6b3c7d5D80C9CFE2eecE6c9 can cause caddress.call to happen; any other caller causes the transaction to revert, whereas the bug allows any caller to proceed.
Any caller other than the privileged sender (0x9797055B68C5DadDE6b3c7d5D80C9CFE2eecE6c9) must cause transfer to revert, but the mutant allows non-privileged callers to succeed.
For any caller, transfer must revert if the caller is not the privileged sender 0x9797055B68C5DadDE6b3c7d5D80C9CFE2eecE6c9; the bug allows any caller to succeed.
For any caller that is not the hardcoded sender 0x9797055B68C5DadDE6b3c7d5D80C9CFE2eecE6c9, transfer(...) must revert; the mutant allows it to succeed.
For any caller, if the call to transfer succeeds, then the caller must be 0x9797055B68C5DadDE6b3c7d5D80C9CFE2eecE6c9; the bug removes this requirement, allowing non-privileged callers to succeed.

For any valid input, the reference contract always transfers the same number of tokens as the length of the recipient array; the buggy version allows an empty recipient list, causing zero transfers where the correct version reverts.

For any input, the reference contract always returns true without reverting only when the recipient array has at least one element; the buggy version violates this by succeeding (returning true) even for an empty recipient array, where the reference correctly reverts.

For any caller that is not the required sender, the reference contract always reverts on the require(msg.sender) check regardless of array lengths; the buggy version violates this by also reverting on that check, so we focus on the required sender where the reference reverts for empty _tos and the mutant succeeds, making the call return true when the reference reverts.
For any call from the required sender, the reference contract reverts on empty _tos while the mutant succeeds, so asserting that a call never returns true when _tos is empty distinguishes them.

For any call from the required sender with any recipient array and values, the reference contract reverts exactly when the recipient array is empty, while the mutant never reverts due to an empty array; the rule asserts that a non-reverting call implies at least one recipient was processed.
